note.note: This cast list has been adapted from the 1679 folio edition of Beaumont and Fletcher’s Fifty Comedies and Tragedies. Spelling has been regularized based on how names appear in the dialogue. Descriptions have been updated.
both presenting a play and therefore launching it, but also the imagery of a boat
nautical term, to the windward side
to avail oneself of (wind) for sailing
clothes to mark someone as grieving
exclamation expressing disgust or indignant reproach
opinion in religion, philosophy, politics, etc.
return to specific place or person
warnings or omens of future events
I’ll not receive thee…a kinder master

Jamie claims that he would not treat Ascanio as a servant, which would be expected given Ascanio’s status as a page, but as a son. There is a certain level of privilage with Jamie’s statement. In terms of Jamie’s authority, he has the ability to treat those who work for him as he pleases. In terms of Ascanio’s status, because he is well-behaved, likely due to a certain level of education, and because he counts on gentlemen as his friends, he will likely be treated differently than other people in a similar role as him.
Referring to la Universidad de Salamanca. It was founded in 1218 and is the oldest university in the Hispanic world.

The lines Here, sweetheart…were more are originally assigned to Milanes, while the lines This is…broker charitable are assigned to Angelo. Since Angelo Milanes is one character, I joined the four lines into a single speech in the modernization.
twig taken from plant or tree to graft or plant
shooting stars facing each other with the potential to crash

Likely a reference to Edmund Spenser’s The Faerie Queene (1590s) in which Spenser imagines a dauther for Pluto, the Greek ruler of the underworld. Spenser calls the daughter Lucifera, which bears a close resembalance to Lucifer, which translates to light bearer.
You have given him a heat

Likely referring to the Ottoman-Habsburg wars, which were fought from the 16th century to the 18th century. The main parties of these wars were the Ottoman Empire and the Habsburg Monarchy, which included a Habsburg-lead Spain
Turkish people regarded collectively; the Turkish power. Also: the Turkish Sultan, the Grand Turk (OED).
Referring to flags (standards) with the image of a moon.
low social status; not of nobility or gentry
Different climates were believed to influence the emotions of people.
person employed to plead a cause for someone else in court
supreme God in the Roman mythology
deep distress arising from some adverse event
youthful, large in stature, and indulgent
completely in love; as in love as one can be
Thou art dead-sick in love, and he’ll pray for thee.

In the first folio, this line is assigned to Leandro. However, since Leandro is the one in love, and has been made fun of by Arsenio in the lines prior, this line should actually be assigned to Arsenio. The line is assigned to Arsenio in the second folio and in Bowers’ scholarly edition, an editorial choice that I agree with and thus have implimented in this modernization.
I will work carefully, cleverly, and head home
Troublesome beauty is the literal translation, but Leandro is referring to Amaranta’s beauty being worth the difficulty of the task of getting to her.

In the first folio, the lines A fools head if I fail and so forsake me. / You shall heare from me daily. are assigned to Arsenio. However, since Leandro is the one attempting to seduce Amaranta, he is the one that could fail. Leandro has also come up with an alternative identity and would be away from Arsenio and Milanes; he promises to give them daily updates here. These lines are assigned to Leandro in the second folio and in Bowers’ scholarly edition, an editorial choice that I agree with and thus have implimented in this modernization.
monetary unity and coin of England
Diego is lamenting that the people of the parish will not die, and thus cannot be buried, which would earn him money.
Diego is referring to the death-bell, a bell tolled to announce a death.
drinks made from hot milk curdled with alcohol often drunk for medicinal purposes
bandages covered in a medicinal substance applied to the skin
Lopez is referring to the wills and funerals that come after people’s death, which benefit him as the Curate.

A raised, enclosed platform in a church or chapel (or sometimes on the outside of the building), sometimes with a canopy and usually with a desk, seat, etc., from which the preacher delivers a sermon, or from which (in some denominations) the officiating minister conducts the service. (OED)
Literally translates to New Spain. Explain the relationship between Spain and the New World.

Cantabit Vacuus is a refrence to the longer Latin phrase, Cantabit vacuus coram latrone viator which translates to the empty-handed traveler sings in front of the robber. Lopez is telling Diego to take the chance in trusting Leandro as they have little to lose.
The character Alonzo Tiveria is character made up by Leandro to trick Diego and Lopez into helping him into Bartolus’ house so he can meet Amaranta.

In the first folio, the lines Good sir, let me think; / I oray ye be patient. are assigned to Leandro’s speech above. However, the second folio assigns the the lines to Lopez, combining the lines previously assigned to Leandro to Lopez’s original lines, Pray ye stay a little, / Nay, let me remember, I beseech ye stay, sir. I decided to follow the second folio’s edits. Turner also changes the lines to follow the second folio’s arrangment.
serious man settled in his character

A form of courtly dramatic entertainment, often richly symbolic, in which music and dancing played a substantial part, costumes and stage machinery tended to be elaborate, and the audience might be invited to contribute to the action or the dancing.
moved a child up and down in their arms or knees
group of people in the service of another

Because, in a later scene, a servant is called by his given name, I decided to do the same elsewhere in the play. This stage direction originally marked an entrance by a Woman-Moore, but I have changed this stage direction and subsequent stage directions and speakers accordingly.
A term of endearment, also used in Shakespeare’s Midsummer Night’s Dream.
(proverb) by locking something up, you can find it quickly.
a good husband, sainted, with an unfaithful wife
Crude joke about Leandro having sex with Amaranta, who, in this line, is equated to a white cow.
Amaranta is observing that Leandro’s choice to study the law and live in such hardship is suspicious.
See introduction to The Spanish Curate
I had forgot my tongue clean
Murrian refers to the flesh of animals that have died die to disease. Lopez is calling the parishioners dead flesh.
piece of clothing worn by a clergyman

Parishioner 3 is talking about the game of bowls, similar in play to bocce ball, in which players take turn throwing or rolling balls to a specific target. The player whose ball is closest to the target wins the round.
To prick a horse means to pierce the foot of a horse with a nail while putting a shoe on the horse, causing lameness.
capons refer to castrated penises. Diego is referring to the men around him as eunuchs, castrated men.
long, white linen robe worn by clergymen
long embroidered cloak worn by clergymen during services
For information about the song and dance, see introduction to The Spanish Curate
refers to a percentage of the revenues of the church that would be used as a clergyman’s stipend.
Octavio claims that they should not be worried about the summoning as there is nothing that the court can take from them.
someone who makes things more difficult than necessary
A scribe could be employed in different ways, with the two most usual ways being a professional worker employed to copy texts or to write down written words.
someone employed to do dirty/unethical work
The assistant asks Don Henrique to explain the purpose of the meeting as he is the one that began the litigation process by hiring Bartolus.
Refers to the practice of mixing pure metals with lesser substances, lessening the quality.

Here, Jacinta is not using rape to necessarily mean sexual assult. Instead, she’s using the term to describe Henrique taking something from her by force. Their previous sexual relationship was dishonest on Henrique’s end, knowing that he had no intentions of marrying her, and Jacinta is again betrayed by Henrique.
produced gathered after reapers (equipment that helps gather produce). Bartolus is painting himself as someone content to only help wealthy clients.
Refering to someone that eagerly sues others.
Violante is claiming that Henrique, through his sexual relationship with Jacinta, came to her bed with empty viens, or, in other words, having used his sperm before they had sex.
fruitful in the sense of having had children.
I follow Turner’s reassigning of this line to Henrique instead of leaving it at the end of Violante’s speech above.
Mythical large reptile who can kill with a single glance.
Do me the pleasure of listening to me
Ascanio is making himself as lowly as possible by stating it would be an honor if he were able to touch the basest part of Violante, her feet.
An avenging god in the Green tradition. Generally used to refer to an avenging/tormenting spirit.
before you visibily age may you have children
Ascanio is referring himself to false in continuing the metaphor of images in this speech. He cannot be a true glass because he is not Violante’s child, and therefore is a illegitimate child.
unprovided for in both means and family

A person suffering from leprosy. Leprosy often caused very visible effects, such as scaliness and scabbiness of the skin. In untreated cases, leprosy can effect sensory and motor function. Because leprosy is such a visible disease, it is commonly used to express repulsion at someone, as Violante does here with Henrique.
A woman that has been disappointed is like a venomous serpent or snake.
monstrous vexed and musty at my chess-play
Amaranta claims Landro is angry at her chess play because he is old fashioned.
If not, do not expect a second offer
been alive for a long time
A person that is both private and frugal saves money.

Lopez is using the example of Milo, a wrestler from the Greek city of Croton. Dated to 6th century B.C.E, Milo was said to have carried a bull on his shoulders. Lopez states that Milo would first carried a calf before he could carry a bull, focusing on the progress of Milo’s strenght to make an analogy of Diego’s supposed wealth.
In smelling food, would overindulge so much that he would have to fast for a month. Lopez is continuing the facade that Diego was a very frugal man, to the point of humor.
Milanes impores Diego to begin the prank they have planned in order to give Leandro time with Amaranta.
The worms must eat first as they are really cheated out of their meals due to their quick work. Diego anticipated that his body will be buried before the rest of his requests are met.

Possible play on 1 Timothy 6:7, For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out (King James Bible). Diego may be using this verse to say that it would be most natural for the poor to remain poor, and thus he’ll leave them nothing.
advice that will cause difference of opinions
Diego would leave the church a new organ, but he believes that the clergymen would steal them.
part of the church near the altar, typically used by clergymen during the service. In older churches, the chancel is typically divided from the rest of the church with a screen or steps.
Diego refers to wanting to give money to teach people to spell, as they write sunt (Latin for they are) as cunt, a slang word referring to female genitals.
each will be given what they need
paper and thread often used to wrap merchandise
Diego is calling doctors and sugeons deceitful, noting that their practices and solutions are so antiquated that they would be found guilty of fraud if tried, and sentenced to death.
the fates, agents that control men’s destinies
those with bad fates according to astrology
Churchyards were typically reserved for the wealthy and religiously-sound, meaning that poor people and criminals were often buried elsewhere.
Diego claims to have a foolish amount of livestock, furniture, land, and other valuables and no-one to leave them to.
The prank is coming to an end, with Diego telling Bartolus to raise the funds from where ever he wishes, as Diego trusts him to do so. Bartolus begins to understand he has been fooled.
confused and become a source of entertainment
I follow the second folio’s reassignment of the line, Do you deserve? from Diego’s speech below to Lopez’s speech here.
Bartolus begins to wonder whether the prank has implications for his wife.
I will get back at you all.
gall bladder. Referring to the imbalance of bile (anger).
Alloy of tin, likely referring to a drum.
previously eaten food. Milanes things Bartolus may throw up.
Amaranta recalls the emberassment of having Leandro fall asleep and snore loudly during a church service.
bundle of sticks tied together for use as fuel. Diego is punning on Bartolus’ actions being heretical to the point of being burnt for this actions.

Ceruse was a white cosmetic used for the skin. Here, Jamie is alluding to Violante’s need to paint her face white because she is the result of her mother’s affair with a man with darker skin than hers (see lines 54-55 below).
a tool used in surveying. Used to take the altitude of the sun.

Originally: a native or inhabitant of ancient Mauretania, a region of North Africa corresponding to parts of present-day Morocco and Algeria. Later usually: a member of a Muslim people of mixed Berber and Arab descent inhabiting north-western Africa (now mainly present-day Mauritania), who in the 8th cent. conquered Spain (OED).
We have both been hurt by Ascanio’s parentage.
I assign these three lines to Bartolus, as the characters on stage played a prank on Bartolus and thus he would be the one to be upset. This change reflects the line assignment in the second folio.
A warrant for my doctor and my silk dealer
person to whom a debt is owed
Leandro is saying that the fair, Amaranta, has saved him.
Violante is referring to Jacinta as a discarded prostitute.
